title: SPEC B review and rewrite: cost, decomposition, stacked PRs

completion_criteria.text: The .claude directory organisation is audited and a target layout decided, with the rename's blast radius enumerated and its execution scoped to a branch outside this thread.
The re-architecture page is copied and rewritten to the narrower main-thread-as-orchestrator scope, with the removed supervisor and orchestrator layer marked as deferred rather than deleted silently.
SPEC B is reviewed line by line against the repository and its wrong or unreproducible citations are corrected, starting with the *_SCHEMA count and the figures no committed script reproduces.
The questions SPEC B leaves open are brainstormed to a decision, above all the instrument source in section 2.2 that section 8 names the single largest open question.
A cited report carrying the corrected architecture, every diagram in it render-verified, and the re-cut gap analysis is produced and REVIEWED by the user, with deferred research left out.
The revised SPEC B is written and approved by the user, superseding the 2026-08-06 document, with every changed claim carrying a citation re-derived at the time of writing.
A successor thread is opened for SPEC B implementation, and this thread closes with no implementation work started.

spine.active_goal: Evaluate mitosis as an OS process owning the control loop and calling agents downward, against the sandboxed-Workflow toolbox, before any of the revised SPEC B is written.
spine.next_step: Open the OS-process approach per 0369. Establish in order: how an OS process would dispatch agents at all, since agent() and parallel() are Workflow hooks it would not have; what else the sandbox provides that it loses; and what it gains, measured against the four toolbox costs this session named. Do NOT resume the section 14 toolbox design or start the SPEC rewrite until that comparison exists. The c5 report render check is still unrun.
spine.last_session: Architecture review in chat only - no files changed and the report render check was not run. Explained the engine and the toolbox, corrected two wrong framings under user challenge, compared against the fanout project, and the user pivoted the thread to the OS-process approach.

open_risks.text: Pair every Part II hypothesis with a fixed quality assertion — the instrument counts tokens and cannot see whether a fused Decompose cuts worse, so a token win carrying a quality regression will read as a success

Name which relation types count as dependency edges before the slice function is specified — contains is 9,380 of 13,689 links and is containment rather than a dependency, and 0365 leaves the relation set as the sole determinant of parallel-safety

Treat the 2026-08-11 directive and the design brief as non-authoritative — the user demoted both as outdated, so requirements come from this thread's decision records and a citation to either carries nothing
Serve the report over HTTP with network access before reviewing it — it loads mermaid from jsdelivr and fonts from Google, so opened as a plain file it shows ten empty diagram frames and looks broken
Instrument for prompt-byte figures or drop them from the SPEC — nothing on disk captures a composed dispatch prompt, so they cannot be derived; the phase and schema counts are now closed
Treat the supervisor, rotation and spawn-cost research as deferred rather than deleted — decisions 0348 to 0351 and section 07 of the report hold it, and it returns only after the engine update

Re-adopt the eight-phase model explicitly in the SPEC rather than citing the 2026-07-30 document — SPEC B's preamble disclaims all citation authority from that document, so a citation to it carries nothing
Read the phase design with git show on branch docs/mitosis-core-rebuild-spec — it was never merged to main, so a working-tree search misses it and wrongly concludes no phase model exists

Have the ENGINE emit the typed record structurally rather than asking any orchestrator to choose to — with the middle layer gone the main thread is the only judge left, which is the soft judgment 0342 refuses to rely on

Keep implementation out of this thread entirely — its criteria are research, artifact and writing only, and a successor thread owns DECOMPOSE_SCHEMA, the slice function and deleting planGroundTruthSeed
Do not switch branches in the primary checkout — live config entries resolve into the release rather than the working tree, so read other branches with git show instead
Never claim mitosis asks a human mid-run — there is no blocking-question primitive in the sandbox, so an escalation parks the unit and surfaces only in the report a human reads after the run returns

Render-verify the pipeline flowchart and the partition sequence diagram before the c5 review — both were edited as text only, and the checks that passed were greps and a tag-nesting parse, never mermaid's own parser
Restore from the backup rather than re-editing if a diagram is broken — the pre-correction report is the only copy of the superseded version and the scratchpad it sits in is session-scoped

Cite mitosis.js for behaviour, never lib/mitosis/*.mjs — mitosis.js has zero imports and calls its own inlined twins, so a run-engine.mjs citation describes a mirror rather than the path that executes
Treat any .claude/lib/superpowers-parallel hit as noise — confirmed untracked and gitignored, so it still answers a grep but describes nothing that runs

Audit plan-to-task-graph's SKILL.md before trusting the pre-implementer census — mitosis.js tells the Parallelize phase to read and follow it, so a codebase-read instruction the census never saw could still be hiding there

Say the workflow JS is sandboxed, never that a subagent is — dispatched agents hold full Bash, Read and Edit, and only the orchestration JS is capability-stripped; the report's wording produced exactly that wrong conclusion this session

Price the rehydration tax on both sides before recommending either architecture — the sandbox cannot read a file, so each fresh invocation pays an agent dispatch just to load state, and the seven Workflow hooks belong to Anthropic and cannot be widened

Start the OS-process comparison from the planners mitosis already owns — derive-edges, wave-planner, derive-clusters and route-planner are deterministic CLIs reached sideways via an agent shelling out, and removing that indirection is the whole gain
Answer how an OS process dispatches agents before adopting one — agent() and parallel() are Workflow hooks, and a process outside the sandbox has no equivalent primitive on hand

Treat refs/mitosis/* and refs/mitosis-manifest/* as permanent remote junk until a retire step exists — nothing found deletes them, and the manifest ref is content-keyed so every spec edit mints another one
A new run overwrites .mitosis/run.json at genesis rather than rotating it — prior-run history is destroyed, so the journal is a durable state channel within a run and not across runs

key_decisions.title: Orchestration leaves the Workflow sandbox for an Agent SDK supervisor process
Zero variance means instructions are binding, not that model output is reproducible
A new SPEC supersedes SPEC B rather than amending it in place
The architecture report is produced and reviewed before the superseding SPEC is written
The rotation trigger is an absolute token count, calibrated before it is fixed
The orchestrator judges inside phases and never reorders, skips or re-runs them
The architecture artifact is a visual-explainer diagram page, not a report-skill deliverable
The rotation threshold is 200K absolute tokens, and the counting field is the open question
Rotation fires at 200,000 tokens of true context occupancy, not input_tokens alone
Orchestrator autonomy is gated on evidence class, and 0330 is amended to permit typed cross-phase re-entry
The eight-phase collapse is re-adopted, re-derived against today's engine, with four amendments
Logbook's progressive-summary spine is rejected as the rotation summarizer
Cross-rotation state is tiered by who can be trusted to author it, not by size
The fresh-session title tax is a real per-spawn charge to model, not an accounting artifact
The supervisor and dispatched orchestrator are cut from scope; the main thread is the orchestrator
Source B is the instrument, it counts four token classes, and attribution is the real gap
SPEC B's residual register is re-cut: only the quality-blindness residual stays open
The SPEC is trusted by provenance, and the codebase is not queried before the implementer phase
Graphify is structurally required in Decompose and its per-cluster subgraphs are passed forward as JSON
Graphify alone determines parallelizability; the confirm-cuts oracle pass is cut
The phase list stays the re-adopted eight-phase model, not the directive's five-step sketch
The report ships CDN-loaded and renumbered, and c5 drops its diagram count
SPEC B is reviewed and rewritten in its own thread before any implementation thread opens
The stale superpowers-parallel tree is renamed to lib/mitosis as a pure move before the SPEC
No mechanism may drop content without leaving a marker that content was dropped
0325's accepted cost is retracted: the SDK host keeps native resume, fork, rewind and a fill sensor
Plain resume is not a rotation, but resumeSessionAt is a measured fill-reducing primitive
The supervisor disables host auto-compaction and owns rotation below the 167,000-token threshold
The engine stays in the Workflow sandbox, so Part III codegen decomposition is live again
The window-fill question is answered at the artifact layer, not the context layer
The SPEC claims a gated dispatch guarantee and names the residual, never tool absence
Spawn depth is closed from existing artifacts: depth 3 is reachable and the new chain is shorter
pillars.md stays a guiding-principles document and carries no measurements
Provenance trust is operationalized by a commit binding plus an admitted-SPEC artifact
The graph slice is computed from graph.json and supplied to the decomposer as input
The 2026-08-11 directive and the design brief are demoted; current decision records govern
Focus shifts to an OS-process control loop; the sandboxed toolbox is no longer the presumed design
The engine leaves the Workflow sandbox; fanout's thesis is adopted, its topology is not
MSP means independently reviewable and green, not independently usable; the stack releases as one

out_of_scope: Implementing any part of SPEC B, which a successor thread owns
Editing SPEC A or the config staging and promotion machinery it shipped
The fix pipeline, excluded by the user from both SPECs
Editing pillars.md at all, including the narrower point-at-tool-routing edit, deferred by the user
